services.name: HVAC system replacement
services.description: Full replacement of a central air conditioner and furnace (or air handler) in a typical single-family home. Includes equipment removal, new system installation, line set replacement where needed, and startup commissioning.

faqs.q: How long does an HVAC replacement take?
faqs.a: Most straight swaps are done in one day; systems requiring duct modifications, line set replacement, or crane access typically take two to three days.

faqs.q: Does replacing my HVAC require a permit?
faqs.a: In nearly all US jurisdictions yes - mechanical and often electrical permits are required, and the final inspection protects your warranty and resale value.

faqs.q: What size system do I need?
faqs.a: Sizing should come from a Manual J load calculation based on your home's square footage, insulation, windows, and climate zone - not from the old unit's tonnage.

faqs.q: Is it cheaper to replace AC and furnace together?
faqs.a: Usually yes: combined replacement avoids duplicate labor and guarantees matched efficiency between components. Expect 10-20% savings versus separate replacements.

services.name: Roof replacement (asphalt shingle)
services.description: Complete tear-off and replacement of asphalt shingle roofing on a roughly 2,000 sq ft single-family home, including underlayment, flashing, and disposal.

sources.label: Remodeling Magazine Cost vs. Value Report

faqs.q: How much does roof replacement cost per square?
faqs.a: Architectural asphalt shingle runs roughly $450-$700 per square (100 sq ft) installed in most metros, with steep pitches, multiple layers, or complex roofs pushing higher.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace my roof?
faqs.a: Most cities and counties require a re-roof permit. It is usually pulled by your contractor and verified at final inspection.

faqs.q: Can you replace a roof in winter?
faqs.a: Yes in most climates - shingles need only adequate sealing temperatures during installation. Expect slightly longer scheduling in cold regions.

faqs.q: Will insurance pay for roof replacement?
faqs.a: Only for covered perils like storm or hail damage, subject to your policy's roof schedule and age rules. Wear-and-tear replacement is not covered.

services.name: Whole-home repipe
services.description: Replacement of supply lines throughout a home, typically PEX for a 1,500-2,500 sq ft house with two bathrooms. Includes drywall patching at access points.

faqs.q: Is PEX or copper better for a repipe?
faqs.a: PEX costs 30-50% less and installs faster; copper lasts longer and adds resale value. Most whole-home repipes now use PEX-A with manifold systems.

faqs.q: Do plumbers need to open walls?
faqs.a: Access holes are cut at fixture connections and run points. Repiping companies include patching, though repaint is typically left to the homeowner.

faqs.q: What triggers a repipe vs repair?
faqs.a: Recurring leaks, polybutylene piping, galvanized corrosion, or slab leak history. If you have had two or more pinhole leaks, replacement is usually cheaper long term.

faqs.q: Is a repipe permit required?
faqs.a: Yes everywhere - plumbing work on supply lines must be permitted and inspected before walls are closed.

services.name: Electrical panel upgrade (200A)
services.description: Upgrade of the main service panel from 100A or less to 200A, including meter base, grounding, utility coordination, and permit inspection.

faqs.q: Why upgrade to 200 amps?
faqs.a: Modern homes with heat pumps, EV chargers, or induction ranges routinely exceed 100A service capacity. Utilities also commonly require 200A for solar interconnection.

faqs.q: How long is the power out?
faqs.a: Typically four to eight hours while the utility disconnects and reconnects service. Your electrician coordinates the utility appointment.

faqs.q: Does the utility charge for this?
faqs.a: Many utilities charge a service-upgrade fee ($100-$600) that is separate from your electrician's quote - ask whether it is included.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit?
faqs.a: Always. Panel work touches the service entrance and must be inspected; unpermitted work can block home sales and void insurance claims.

services.name: Interior painting (whole home)
services.description: Two-coat premium acrylic repaint of walls, ceilings, and trim in a roughly 2,000 sq ft home including prep, masking, and cleanup.

faqs.q: How do painters price jobs?
faqs.a: Most quote per square foot of floor area ($1.90-$3.50) or per room. Height, trim density, and repair work move quotes up from the base rate.

faqs.q: Does painting require a permit?
faqs.a: No - cosmetic painting does not require permits anywhere in the US.

faqs.q: Should I buy the paint myself?
faqs.a: Let the contractor supply it: pros get trade discounts that offset their margin, and they warranty coverage and finish quality only when materials are theirs.

faqs.q: When is exterior season?
faqs.a: Exterior paint needs surfaces above ~50°F overnight. In cold-winter states exterior work concentrates April-October; interiors are year-round.
